messages.author: bba576a74eafc909
messages.subject: Model predictions
parts:
Hi,

My question relates to Wallace, but more directly to the ENMeval package it uses. 

If I select "crossvalidate" with 10 replicates in the MaxEnt GUI, the output prediction is given as a mean (and median, min, max) of 10 replicate runs.

For ENMeval, Muscarella et al.(2014) says the "‘random k‐fold’ method [is]...equivalent to the ‘cross‐validate’ partitioning scheme available in the current version of the Maxent software".

So, if I select "random k-fold" with folds=10 in Wallace/ENMeval for a model, is the prediction output also a mean (or some summary) of 10 replicate runs? The ENMeval manual suggests not, that the prediction raster that can be obtained for a given model is on unpartitioned data. So does that mean the prediction is from one replicate using all data?

Or am I misunderstanding?

Thanks,
Amy

messages.author: fe049c2835236bb1
messages.subject: Re: Model predictions
parts:
Amy,

Yes, sorry for the confusion. ENMeval makes a single random k-fold partition, then does cross validation for those k folds. It does no replicates in the function, but you can do this by simply running ENMevaluate() or the associated module in Wallace again. Hope this answers your question.

Jamie

messages.author: fe049c2835236bb1
messages.subject: Re: Model predictions
parts:
Yes, that is correct. The model prediction is always made from the full occurrence dataset in ENMeval. The partitioning and cross validation is done only to make evaluations on test data, and the corresponding statistics are meant to aid the user in selecting optimal model settings. Thus, selection of partition method will not affect the model prediction, just the evaluation statistics.

Jamie
